div.l: And haue a þanke and ȝet a cote ⁊and and a · hode
In ȝouthe he hadde lerned a gode mestere
He was a · wel god wriȝt a · Carpentere
This Reue satte vp on a ful good stot
Þat was al pomely gray and highte scot
A · long surcote of peers vppon he hade
And by his side he bare a rusti blade
Of Northfolk was þis Reue of whiche I telle
By side a · toun men clepen it baldeswelle
Tukked he was as is a frere a bowte
And · euer he roode þe hyndrest of on Route
¶ A · Somynour was þer wᵗith vs in · þat place
Þat hadde a · fyri cherubynnes face
For sausefleme he was with eyghen narwe
Als hoote he was and lecherous as a sparwe
Wit scalled browes blak ⁊and pilid berde
Of his visage children weren a ferde
Ther nas quyke siluer litarge or bremston
Boras orsure ne oyle of tartre noon
Ne oynement þat wold clense ⁊and bite
Þat hym myghte helpe of his whelkes white
For of þe knobbes sittyng in his chekes
Wel loued he garlik oynons ⁊and eke lekes
And for to drink strong wyn rede as blode
Than wold he spek and crie as he were wode
And whan þat he wel dronken hade the wyn
Þan wold he speke no word but latyn
A · few t̉ermes hade he two or thre
Þat he hade lerned out of som de cre
No wonder is he herd it al the day
And eke ȝe knowen wel how þat a · Iay
Kan clepe watte as wel as con the pope
But ho so couthe in other þing him grope
Þan hade he spent al his philosophie
Ay questio quid Iurꝭes wold he crye
He was a gentel harlot and a · kynd
A · better felowe Shul men not fynde
